name: Low-Speed Electric Bicycle
description: A device with a saddle or seat, two or three wheels, fully operable pedals and an electric motor producing no more than 750 watts, in one of three classes: Class 1 and Class 3 pedal-assist up to 20 and 28 mph, and Class 2 motor-propelled up to 20 mph. Defined by Iowa Code §321.1(36A), as amended by SF 490 (2026), and regulated by §321.235B.
restrictions: A saddle or seat, two or three wheels, fully operable pedals, and a motor producing no more than 750 watts; before SF 490 took effect on July 1, 2026 the motor had to be under 750 watts
Class 1 assists only while the rider pedals and stops at 20 mph; Class 2's motor can propel it alone, up to 20 mph; Class 3 assists only while pedaling and stops at 28 mph
The motor assist must stop when the rider stops pedaling, applies the brakes or disengages the motor
Class 3 may not be ridden without a speedometer showing its speed in miles per hour
Manufactured and equipped to the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512)
Carries a permanent label, in at least 9-point Arial, stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage
No one may knowingly modify its speed capability or motor engagement so it no longer fits a class, and anyone who modifies it must affix a new label
Class 3 riders must be 16 or older; a younger rider may ride on one as a passenger
Counts as a bicycle, and its rider has a bicycle rider's rights and duties on the road
May be ridden anywhere a bicycle may, including streets, highways, shoulders, bike lanes, bikeways and multi-use paths
On a bike lane or multi-use path, a Class 3 may go no faster than the posted limit, or 20 mph where none is posted
Not subject to vehicle licensing, registration, titling, inspection or proof of insurance, and needs no driver's license or permit
